newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 28.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
* Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc, the largest Coke bottler, has agreed to acquire bottling companies from the Coca-Cola Co in Canada and New York for $1.66 billion in cash and assumed debt.
* Consumer confidence hit a 28-year high in May.
* Treasury prices dropped, sending the yield on the 30-year bond to 7.02 percent from 6.98 percent.
* News Corp Ltd has reached a tentative agreement to join the satellite TV venture of Primestar Partners.
* Video game maker Sega Enterprises Ltd and toy maker Bandai Co Ltd cancelled their planned merger.

* The Supreme Court has turned down an appeal from the accounting firm of Ernst & Young of a ruling that allowed partners who did not exercise management responsibility to be protected by federal labor and anti-discrimination laws normally afforded rank-and-file employees.
* Nissan Motor Co Ltd reported its first annual profit in five years.
* Interpublic Group of Cos Inc has acquired a 10 percent stake in Tripod Inc, an interactive marketing and media company, for $2.5 million.
* Smith Barney has suspended Robert Maloney, the director of its Northeast region, as an investigation is conducted into his role in soliciting campaign contributions, unnamed sources said.
* Credit Suisse First Boston has bought 55 Wall Street for $21 million and plans to turn it into a ballroom, and possibly apartments or a hotel.

* Wall Street analysts and investors believe Donna Karan, chief executive of Donna Karan International Inc, has been spending too much money and that the company is due for some cost-cutting initiatives.
* CUC International Inc and HFS Inc have reached a definitive agreement to merge in a deal valued at about $11 billion.
* AT&T Corp is in merger talks with SBC Communications Inc, a deal that would join two telecommunications giants, sources said.
